question: What is a DNS TTL, and how does this resolver's cache count it down when it hands records back?
answer_hinglish:
TTL (time to live) har resource record ke saath aata hai, seconds mein: zone ka owner bolta hai 'is answer ko itni der tak yaad rakh sakte ho, uske baad mujhse phir poochna'. Resolver ka cache isi number se decide karta hai ki record kab tak valid hai.

Is project mein Cache.putRRset TTL ko seconds se absolute time mein badal deta hai: expiresAt = now() + ttl * 1000 (milliseconds). Record ke saath original TTL store nahi hota, sirf expiry ka moment. Jab getRRset padhta hai, toh left = expiresAt - now() nikalta hai; left <= 0 hai toh entry wahi delete hoti hai aur undefined milta hai (lazy expiry -- koi background timer nahi). Warna har record ki copy mein ttl = Math.floor(left / 1000) daala jaata hai.

Countdown kyun zaroori hai? Kyunki hum ek recursive resolver hain aur stub client (nslookup, OS) ko answer aage dete hain. Agar 300 s wala record 290 s pehle cache hua tha aur hum client ko phir se 300 bolein, toh client usse 300 s aur rakhega -- record apni asli umar se lagbhag double jee lega. Isliye client ko sirf bacha hua time milta hai.

Test 'an RRset lives for its smallest TTL, and reads count the TTL down' yahi dikhata hai: 100 s ka set, 40 s baad read par TTL 60, 99 s baad bhi 2 records, 100 s par undefined, aur cache.size 0 -- expired entry read par hi hat gayi.
why_needed: Bina TTL ke cache ko pata hi nahi chalega ki data kab purana ho gaya; aur bina countdown ke downstream caches record ko uski allowed umar se zyada rakhenge.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan par doodh ka packet: expiry date likhi hai. Dukaandaar customer ko 'aaj se 7 din' nahi bolta, packet par jo date bachi hai wahi batata hai.
how_it_works: putRRset: ttl -> expiresAt = now + ttl*1000. getRRset: left = expiresAt - now; left <= 0 -> delete + undefined; else ttl = floor(left/1000) har returned copy par.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts mein Cache.putRRset aur Cache.getRRset. Time injected clock se aata hai (CacheOptions.now, default Date.now). test/cache.test.ts ka clock() helper time ko haath se aage badhata hai. Mutation C1 (positive entries never expire) 3 tests ne pakda.
advantages: Absolute expiry store karne se countdown ek subtraction hai
Koi timer nahi, koi background thread nahi
Client ko sahi bacha hua TTL milta hai
disadvantages: Expired entries tab tak memory mein rehti hain jab tak koi unhe padhe ya eviction unhe nikale
Math.floor ki wajah se aakhri second mein client ko TTL 0 milta hai
common_mistakes: Client ko original TTL lauta dena
TTL ko seconds mein expiry time ki tarah store karna aur ms clock se compare karna
Har entry ke liye setTimeout lagana
follow_up_questions: Lazy expiry ke bajaye periodic sweep kab behtar hoga?
Math.floor ki jagah Math.ceil lagane se kya badlega?
Clock peeche chala jaye (NTP adjust) toh kya hoga?

question: Why does the cache store whole RRsets keyed by (name, type) instead of single records, and why is the key case-insensitive?
answer_hinglish:
DNS mein sabse chhoti meaningful unit RRset hai: ek name, ek type, ek class ke saare records saath. Jaise www.alpha.test ke do A records (192.0.2.80 aur 192.0.2.81) ek hi RRset hain. Server poora set bhejta hai, aur client ko bhi poora set milna chahiye -- aadha set dena galat answer hai, kyunki client ko lagega ki sirf ek hi address hai.

Isliye Cache.putRRset ek array leta hai (sab records same name aur type ke) aur ek hi key ke neeche store karta hai: posKey(name, type) = canonicalName(name) + '|' + type. getRRset bhi poora set lauta deta hai. Resolver mein groupRRsets function response ke records ko name|type se group karta hai, phir har group ek baar putRRset hota hai -- toh cache mein kabhi aadha set nahi pahunchta.

Case-insensitive kyun? DNS names case-insensitive hain (RFC 4343): WWW.Test aur www.TEST ek hi naam hain. Agar key raw string hoti toh ek hi naam ki do entries ban jaati, ek purani rehti, aur hit rate girta. canonicalName ASCII lowercase karta hai, isliye test 'lookups are case-insensitive' mein WWW.Test daal kar www.TEST se mil jaata hai.

Class key mein nahi hai, kyunki resolver sirf IN class ke records cache karta hai (classify mein isIn filter).
why_needed: Answers ko sahi aur poora rakhne ke liye cache ki unit wahi honi chahiye jo protocol ki unit hai.
real_world_analogy: Library mein ek kitaab ke saare volumes ek hi shelf label ke neeche rakhte hain; agar volume 2 kisi aur shelf par ho toh reader sochega series mein ek hi volume hai.
how_it_works: groupRRsets(answers) -> Map<name|type, records[]> -> har set putRRset(set, rank). Key: posKey = canonicalName(name)|type. getRRset(name, type) same key banata hai.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts mein posKey aur nxKey arrow functions; src/resolver.ts mein groupRRsets aur cacheAnswers. Test: cache.test.ts 'lookups are case-insensitive'.
advantages: Client ko hamesha poora set milta hai
Ek naam ki ek hi entry, case se farak nahi
Key ek simple string, Map mein O(1) lookup
disadvantages: Ek bhi record badle toh poora set replace hota hai
Class key mein nahi; IN ke alawa class kabhi cache nahi hogi
common_mistakes: Har record alag key se cache karna
Name ko lowercase kiye bina key banana
Different responses ke records ko ek set mein merge kar dena
follow_up_questions: Ek hi set ke records alag TTL ke saath aayein toh kya karoge?
Non-ASCII bytes wale label ka canonical form kaise banta hai?

question: When the records in one RRset arrive with different TTLs, which TTL does the cache use and why?
answer_hinglish:
Sabse chhota TTL. Cache.putRRset mein ttl = Math.min(this.maxTtl, ...rrs.map((r) => r.ttl)) hai -- set ke saare records ka minimum, upar se maxTtl ka cap.

RFC 2181 section 5.2 bolta hai ki ek RRset ke saare records ka TTL barabar hona chahiye. Lekin real duniya mein galat configured zones alag TTL bhej dete hain. Tab choice hai: pehle record ka, sabse bade ka, ya sabse chhote ka. Sabse chhota safe hai, kyunki zone owner ne kisi ek record ke liye bola 'isse sirf 100 s rakho'. Bada TTL lene ka matlab us record ko owner ki marzi se zyada der rakhna. Chhota lene ka nuksaan sirf ek extra upstream query hai -- correctness ke liye sasta.

Poore set ka ek hi expiresAt hota hai, aur getRRset har record ko same bacha hua TTL deta hai. Isliye test 'an RRset lives for its smallest TTL, and reads count the TTL down' mein 300 aur 100 wale records dono 100 dikhate hain, 40 s baad dono 60.

Mutation C2 ne yeh rule toda: TTL pehle record se lo (300 wala). Ek test fail hua -- yahi unit test. Note: test ne jaan bujh kar 300 wala record pehle rakha hai, warna 'pehla record' aur 'sabse chhota' same nikalte aur mutant bach jaata.
why_needed: Inconsistent zone data par bhi owner ki sabse sakht expiry ka respect karna.
real_world_analogy: Group mein teen dost movie jaa rahe hain; ek ko 9 baje ghar pahunchna hai. Group 9 baje tak hi bahar rehta hai, kyunki sabse jaldi wala time sab par lagta hai.
how_it_works: rrs.map(ttl) -> Math.min(maxTtl, ...) -> ttl <= 0 toh store nahi -> expiresAt = now + ttl*1000 -> ek expiry poore set ki.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts Cache.putRRset. Test cache.test.ts 'an RRset lives for its smallest TTL, and reads count the TTL down'. README mutation table: C2 (RRset TTL taken from the first record, not the smallest) -> 1 test failed.
advantages: Owner ki sabse sakht expiry respect hoti hai
Ek set, ek expiry -- simple
Test order se mutant ko pakadna possible hua
disadvantages: Ek galat chhote TTL wala record poore set ko jaldi expire karta hai
Original alag-alag TTLs ki jaankari kho jaati hai
common_mistakes: Pehle record ka TTL le lena
Test mein chhota TTL pehle rakh dena (mutant bach jaata hai)
Har record ka alag expiry rakhna aur aadha set lautana
follow_up_questions: Test data ka order mutation testing ke liye kyun matter karta hai?
RFC 2181 ke hisaab se server ko alag TTLs bhejne chahiye kya?

question: What does a TTL of 0 mean, and why does the cache cap every TTL at maxTtl (one day by default)?
answer_hinglish:
TTL 0 ka matlab hai 'yeh answer abhi ek baar use karo, cache mat karo'. Zone owners isse use karte hain jab answer har request par badal sakta hai. Cache.putRRset mein ttl <= 0 hote hi false return hota hai aur kuch store nahi hota. Answer phir bhi client ko jaata hai (resolver usse direct lauta deta hai), bas yaad nahi rakha jaata.

Doosri taraf, TTL field 32-bit hai, toh koi server 2,000,000,000 seconds (60+ saal) bhi bhej sakta hai -- galti se ya jaan bujh kar. Agar hum woh maan lein, toh ek galat ya poisoned record process restart tak pinned reh jaata hai. Isliye har positive TTL ko maxTtl se cap kiya jaata hai: Math.min(this.maxTtl, ...ttls), default 86400 s (1 din). Negative answers ka alag cap hai, maxNegativeTtl, default 10800 s (3 ghante).

Test 'TTL 0 is never cached; a huge TTL is capped at maxTtl' dono dikhata hai: maxTtl 3600 ke saath TTL 0 wala putRRset false deta hai; 2_000_000_000 wala record read par 3600 dikhata hai aur 3600 s baad gayab.

Mutation C7 (TTL 0 cached) aur C8 (no maxTtl cap) dono ek-ek test ne pakde.
why_needed: TTL 0 ka respect na karna owner ke intent ko todta hai; cap na hone se ek kharab TTL cache ko hamesha ke liye zehreela bana sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ki prescription: 'sirf aaj ek goli' (TTL 0) -- stock nahi karna. Aur pharmacy kabhi koi dawai 1 saal se zyada shelf par nahi rakhti, chahe box par 60 saal likha ho.
how_it_works: putRRset: ttl = min(maxTtl, ...ttls); if ttl <= 0 return false; else store with expiresAt. CacheOptions.maxTtl default 86_400.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts Cache constructor (maxTtl ?? 86_400, maxNegativeTtl ?? 10_800) aur putRRset. Test cache.test.ts 'TTL 0 is never cached; a huge TTL is capped at maxTtl'. README mutations C7 aur C8.
advantages: Owner ka 'do not cache' intent maana jaata hai
Galat ya hostile TTL ka nuksaan max 1 din
Cap configurable hai
disadvantages: Jo zone sach mein 1 hafte ka TTL chahta hai usse bhi roz phir poocha jaata hai
TTL 0 wale naam har baar upstream jaate hain (load)
common_mistakes: TTL 0 ko 'hamesha' samajh lena
Cap sirf positive par lagana aur negative ko bhool jaana
TTL ko signed int padhna (RFC 2181 ke hisaab se top bit set ho toh 0 maanna chahiye)
follow_up_questions: Bade resolvers (Unbound, BIND) ka default max TTL kya hota hai aur kyun configurable hai?
TTL 0 answer CNAME chain ke beech mein ho toh kya hoga?

question: How does negative caching work here (RFC 2308), and why is NXDOMAIN cached per name while NODATA is cached per name and type?
answer_hinglish:
Negative caching ka matlab hai 'yeh cheez exist nahi karti' ko bhi kuch der yaad rakhna, taaki har baar root se zone tak poocha na pade. Do alag negative answers hain. NXDOMAIN: naam hi exist nahi karta -- kisi bhi type ke liye. NODATA: naam exist karta hai (rcode NOERROR), lekin us type ka record nahi hai, jaise mail.alpha.test ka A hai par AAAA nahi.

Kyunki NXDOMAIN poore naam ke baare mein hai, Cache.putNegative usse nxKey(name) = name|NX ke neeche rakhta hai -- type key mein nahi. Baad mein us naam ka MX, TXT, kuch bhi poocho, getNegative pehle nxKey dekhta hai aur hit deta hai. NODATA sirf us ek type ke baare mein hai, toh woh posKey(name, type) par jaata hai; A poocho toh miss, aur upstream query jaati hai. Agar NODATA ko per name cache karte toh A record bhi 'nahi hai' bol dete -- galat answer.

Resolver tests yeh end-to-end saabit karte hain: 'NXDOMAIN is cached for the SOA minimum (60 s) and covers other types of the same name' (A ke baad MX 0 queries) aur 'NODATA is cached per type: another type of the same name is still asked' (AAAA 0 queries, A 1 query).

Mutation C4 (NXDOMAIN cached per type) 2 tests ne pakda. Ek aur detail: kisi naam ka positive RRset aate hi putRRset us naam ka nxKey aur usi type ka NODATA entry delete karta hai -- 'learning a record for a name clears an old negative entry for it'.
why_needed: Bina negative caching ke typo wale ya missing naam (aur AAAA jo bahut zones mein nahi hota) har baar poori resolution chalate hain -- authoritative servers par bekaar load.
real_world_analogy: Phone directory: 'is naam ka koi insaan shehar mein nahi hai' (NXDOMAIN) toh uska mobile, landline, email sab nahi. 'Insaan hai par landline nahi hai' (NODATA) -- mobile phir bhi ho sakta hai.
how_it_works: classify: rcode NXDOMAIN -> putNegative(name, type, 'NXDOMAIN', soa) -> key name|NX. NOERROR + koi answer/referral nahi -> putNegative(..., 'NODATA', soa) -> key name|type. getNegative: [nxKey, posKey] order mein check.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts putNegative, getNegative, NegativeKind. src/resolver.ts classify dono kinds likhta hai; resolveOne cache se negative hit ko rcode NXDOMAIN ya NOERROR mein badalta hai. Unit test 'negative TTL = min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum); NXDOMAIN covers every type, NODATA only one'.
advantages: NXDOMAIN ek entry se saare types cover karta hai
NODATA galti se doosre types ko block nahi karta
SOA bhi store hota hai, toh client ko authority section mil jaata hai
disadvantages: NXDOMAIN ke neeche ke naamon (RFC 8020) ko cover nahi karta -- har child naam alag poocha jaata hai
Galat NXDOMAIN aaya toh woh bhi TTL tak yaad rehta hai
common_mistakes: NODATA ko NXDOMAIN ki tarah per-name cache karna
Negative answer ko SOA ke bina cache karna
Positive data aane par purana negative entry na hatana
follow_up_questions: RFC 8020 (NXDOMAIN: there really is nothing underneath) se kya fayda hota?
Empty non-terminal ko NODATA kyun maana jaata hai?
CNAME jiska target missing hai, uska cache entry kaisa dikhega?

question: How is the TTL of a negative cache entry computed, and why is a negative answer without an SOA not cached at all?
answer_hinglish:
Negative TTL = min(SOA record ka TTL, SOA ka minimum field, maxNegativeTtl). Code: Math.min(soa.ttl, soa.data.minimum, this.maxNegativeTtl). Result <= 0 hai toh kuch store nahi hota, aur function 0 lautata hai; warna jo TTL use hua woh lautata hai.

Kyun SOA? Negative answer mein koi record nahi hota jiska TTL lein. RFC 2308 section 5 bolta hai ki authoritative server authority section mein zone ka SOA bhejta hai, aur negative answer ki umar SOA ke TTL aur uske MINIMUM field ka chhota wala hai. MINIMUM field ka matlab RFC 2308 ne yahi bana diya (pehle kuch aur tha). Dono ka minimum isliye ki agar SOA khud 60 s mein expire hota hai, toh uske base par diya gaya negative answer usse zyada nahi jee sakta.

maxNegativeTtl default 10800 s (3 ghante) -- RFC 2308 yahi cap suggest karta hai, kyunki galat NXDOMAIN bahut der tak rehna dangerous hai (naya record add kiya, users ko dikhta hi nahi).

SOA nahi hai toh cache nahi: bina SOA ke humein pata hi nahi ki kitni der rakhein; koi default TTL ghadna guess hoga. Isliye putNegative mein pehli line hai: !soa ya kind SOA nahi -> return 0. Tests: 'a negative answer without an SOA is not cached; negative TTL is capped at maxNegativeTtl' (undefined SOA -> 0; SOA 86400/86400 ke saath cap 100 -> 100) aur fixture mein alpha.test ka SOA minimum 60, TTL 300 -> NXDOMAIN 60 s. Mutations C3 (SOA minimum ignore) 2 tests, C10 (no-SOA cached with default TTL) 1 test.
why_needed: Negative answer ki umar zone owner ke control mein honi chahiye, aur bina jaankari ke kuch bhi cache karna guesswork hai.
real_world_analogy: 'Stock khatam hai' board: dukaandaar likhta hai 'agle hafte tak' (SOA minimum). Agar board par koi date hi nahi, toh hum usse yaad nahi rakhte, kal phir pooch lete hain.
how_it_works: putNegative(name, type, kind, soa): soa missing -> 0; ttl = min(soa.ttl, soa.data.minimum, maxNegativeTtl); ttl <= 0 -> 0; key choose; negative.set({kind, soa copy, expiresAt}); evict(); return ttl.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts Cache.putNegative. Resolver ka classify sirf woh SOA deta hai jo zone ke andar ho aur jiske neeche query ka naam ho (isSubdomain(name, rr.name)), warna soa undefined -> not cached. test/fakenet.ts ka SOA(origin, minimum, ttl) helper fixtures banata hai.

3 ghante ka cap galat NXDOMAIN ka nuksaan bound karta hai
Return value test ko seedha TTL check karne deta hai
disadvantages: SOA bhoolne wala server har baar poocha jaata hai
Bailiwick ke bahar ka SOA ignore hota hai, toh kuch negatives cache nahi honge
common_mistakes: Sirf SOA ka TTL lena aur minimum field bhool jaana
No-SOA case mein koi default TTL laga dena
maxTtl (1 din) ko negative par bhi laga dena, alag 3 ghante ka cap nahi

SOA minimum field ka purana matlab kya tha?

question: If you think of the resolver cache as a small key-value database, what are its tables, keys, values and expiry model?
answer_hinglish:
Cache ek in-memory key-value store hai jisme do 'tables' hain, dono JavaScript Map. Pehli: positive -- key posKey = canonicalName|type, value PositiveEntry { rrs, expiresAt, rank }. Doosri: negative -- key ya toh nxKey = canonicalName|NX (NXDOMAIN, poora naam) ya posKey (NODATA, naam + type), value NegativeEntry { kind, soa, expiresAt }.

Do Maps kyun, ek kyun nahi? NODATA aur positive RRset same key format share karte hain (name|type). Ek hi Map mein hote toh ek doosre ko overwrite karte, aur get karte waqt har baar type check karna padta. Alag Maps mein key collision possible hi nahi, aur getRRset kabhi galti se negative entry nahi lautata.

Expiry model: har row mein absolute expiresAt (ms). Koi TTL index ya sweeper nahi -- expiry lazy hai: getRRset / getNegative padhte waqt expired row delete karte hain. Yeh Redis ke lazy expire jaisa hai, lekin Redis ki tarah random sampling se active expiry nahi hai.

Write rules (constraints) bhi database jaise hain: rank column ek 'priority' hai -- referral row ek unexpired answer row ko overwrite nahi kar sakti. Positive insert ek 'trigger' chalata hai: usi naam ka NX row aur usi name|type ka NODATA row delete. Capacity: maxEntries (default 10000) dono Maps ka total; full hone par insertion order se sabse purani row evict.

Values copies hain: putRRset aur getRRset dono copyData se naya object banate hain, toh bahar ka code stored row ko mutate nahi kar sakta.
why_needed: Cache ko data store ki tarah sochne se uske invariants (keys, constraints, expiry, capacity) saaf dikhte hain aur bugs pakadna aasaan hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek register mein do alag pages: 'kya hai' wali list aur 'kya nahi hai' wali list. Dono mein naam same ho sakte hain, isliye alag pages rakhte hain taaki ek entry doosri ko mita na de.
how_it_works: positive: Map<name|type, {rrs, expiresAt, rank}>. negative: Map<name|NX or name|type, {kind, soa, expiresAt}>. size = positive.size + negative.size. evict() jab size > maxEntries.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts: interfaces PositiveEntry aur NegativeEntry, Maps positive aur negative, posKey/nxKey, get size(), clear(). Tests cache.test.ts 'cache: unit' block. Persistence nahi hai: restart = khaali cache.
advantages: O(1) get/put
Key collision impossible (alag Maps)
Expiry ka koi background kaam nahi
disadvantages: Sirf ek process ki memory, restart par sab gaya
Expired rows padhe jaane tak jagah gherti hain
Byte size ka koi hisaab nahi, sirf entries ki ginti
common_mistakes: NODATA aur positive ko ek Map mein rakhna
Relative TTL store karna aur har read par 'kab store hua tha' alag se rakhna
Bahar ko internal object reference de dena
follow_up_questions: Is cache ko Redis mein le jaana ho toh key aur expiry design kaise hoga?
maxEntries ki jagah bytes se limit kaise lagaoge?
Lazy expiry ke saath memory leak jaisa behaviour kab dikhega?

question: What is cache ranking (referral vs answer), and how does it stop glue and NS data from poisoning real answers?
answer_hinglish:
Ranking ka matlab hai har cached RRset ke saath likhna ki woh kahan se aaya, aur us source par kitna bharosa hai. Is project mein do ranks hain (RFC 2181 5.4.1 ka chhota version): 'referral' -- referral response ke authority section ka NS set aur additional section ka glue; aur 'answer' -- authoritative server ke answer section se aaya data. RANK_ORDER mein referral = 1, answer = 2.

Problem kya hai? Glue woh data hai jo parent zone apne child ke baare mein bolta hai -- yeh child ka authoritative answer nahi hai. Parent ka glue purana ya galat ho sakta hai, aur attacker referral mein glue chipka kar sabse aasaani se data inject karta hai (Kaminsky attack ka 'extra records' hissa). Agar glue ek sahi answer ko overwrite kar de, ya client ko answer ki tarah diya jaye, toh poisoning ka raasta khul jaata hai.

Do rules: (1) putRRset mein: purana entry unexpired hai aur uska rank naye se bada hai -> return false, overwrite nahi. Answer referral ko replace kar sakta hai, ulta nahi. (2) getRRset ka minRank default 'answer' hai; referral entry us check par undefined deti hai. Resolver ka resolveOne 'answer' se padhta hai, sirf closestServers aur cachedAddresses 'referral' minRank se padhte hain (servers dhoondhne ke liye).

Tests: unit 'referral data does not overwrite an unexpired answer, and is not returned as an answer', aur resolver test 'referral data (NS and glue) is cached at low rank: never returned as an answer' (ns1.alpha.test ka A glue se pata hai, phir bhi client ke liye authority se poocha jaata hai). Mutations C5 (1 test), C6 (2), R7 glue cached at answer rank (1).
why_needed: Bailiwick filter ke baad bhi parent ka data child ke data se kam bharosemand hai; ranking yeh fark cache mein zinda rakhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Padosi ne bataya 'Sharma ji ka number yeh hai' (glue) -- kaam chalane ke liye theek. Lekin Sharma ji ne khud apna number diya (answer) toh padosi ki baat usse kabhi nahi badlegi, aur kisi teesre ko hum padosi wala number 'official' bata kar nahi denge.
how_it_works: putRRset(rrs, rank): old && old.expiresAt > now && RANK_ORDER[old.rank] > RANK_ORDER[rank] -> false. getRRset(name, type, minRank='answer'): RANK_ORDER[e.rank] < RANK_ORDER[minRank] -> undefined.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts Rank, RANK_ORDER, putRRset, getRRset. src/resolver.ts classify referral case mein putRRset(nsSet, 'referral') aur glue sets 'referral'; cacheAnswers 'answer'. closestServers getRRset(zone, TYPE.NS, 'referral').
advantages: Glue se sahi answer kabhi nahi badalta
Client ko kabhi unverified glue answer ki tarah nahi milta
Sirf do ranks: samajhna aur test karna aasaan
disadvantages: Referral entry jo answer ke liye padhi gayi, cache mein jagah gherti rehti hai
RFC 2181 ke poore ranks (authoritative vs non-authoritative answer, additional) nahi hain
Expired answer ke baad glue use replace kar deta hai (theek hai, lekin same key ab low rank hai)
common_mistakes: Default minRank 'referral' rakhna
Glue ko cacheAnswers se store kar dena
Rank check expiry check ke bina karna (expired answer referral ko hamesha block karega)
follow_up_questions: Bailiwick aur ranking mein kya fark hai -- dono kyun chahiye?
RFC 2181 5.4.1 ke baaki ranks kaun se hain?
DNSSEC hone par ranking ki zaroorat kam hogi kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Do ranks simplicity dete hain; keemat yeh hai ki AA=1 answer aur non-authoritative answer (jaise CNAME chase mein aaya target) ek hi rank par hain.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi naya code path glue ko 'answer' rank par likh de (R7), toh glue client tak pahunchega; isi liye resolver test ns1.alpha.test ko authority se poochna assert karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: RFC 2181 ke 7 levels jaise multi-level trust; DNSSEC validation (is project mein implement nahi hai) jisme signature trust deta hai; glue ko alag 'hint' store mein rakhna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Ranking ka cost per write ek comparison hai, scale par koi asar nahi. 100x par bada sawaal cache ka shared/sharded hona hai; rank tab bhi entry ke saath travel karna chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Authoritative answer (AA=1) ko alag top rank, poisoning attempts ka counter (rejected overwrites), aur DNSSEC -- jo asli fix hai aur yahan implement nahi hai.

question: Walk through Cache.putRRset line by line: what does each step do and which test pins it?
answer_hinglish:
putRRset(rrs, rank) ek RRset store karta hai aur boolean lautata hai ki store hua ya nahi. Step by step:

1) const first = rrs[0]; khaali array toh false. 2) ttl = Math.min(this.maxTtl, ...ttls) -- sabse chhota TTL, 1 din ka cap. 3) ttl <= 0 toh false (TTL 0 cache nahi). 4) key = posKey(first.name, first.type) -- first ka naam aur type poore set ki pehchaan hai, kyunki caller (groupRRsets) guarantee karta hai ki set ek naam-type ka hai. 5) Rank guard: purana unexpired entry zyada rank ka hai toh false. 6) this.positive.delete(key) phir set -- yeh delete jaan bujh kar hai: JS Map mein existing key ko set karne se uska position nahi badalta. Delete + set se refresh hua entry Map ke end par jaata hai, toh Map order = age order, aur evict() hamesha sabse purana nikaal sakta hai. 7) Value mein records ki copy (copyData) aur expiresAt = now + ttl*1000. 8) Positive data aaya toh is naam ka NXDOMAIN entry aur is name|type ka NODATA entry delete -- woh ab jhooth hain. 9) evict(). 10) return true.

Har step ka test cache.test.ts mein hai: smallest TTL (C2), TTL 0 aur cap (C7, C8), ranking (C5), 'learning a record for a name clears an old negative entry for it', 'when full, the oldest entry is evicted', aur 'returned records are copies'.

Ek honest note: step 8 sirf usi type ka NODATA hatata hai; doosre types ke NODATA entries sahi bane rehte hain, kyunki ek naya A record AAAA ke 'nahi hai' ko galat nahi karta.
why_needed: Yeh function cache ke saare write-side invariants ek jagah rakhta hai; interview mein ise line by line samjha paana dikhata hai ki design intentional hai.
real_world_analogy: Godown mein naya maal rakhna: expiry check, 'do not store' label check, VIP maal ko normal maal se replace na karna, purana stock aage se hatana, 'out of stock' board utaarna, aur jagah bhar gayi toh sabse purana nikaalna.
how_it_works: first -> ttl min/cap -> ttl<=0? -> key -> rank guard -> delete+set (age order) -> clear NX + NODATA -> evict -> true.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts Cache.putRRset, evict, copyData. Caller: src/resolver.ts cacheAnswers aur classify ka referral branch.

Boolean return se test aur caller dono ko pata chalta hai
Map order trick se eviction O(1)
disadvantages: Caller par bharosa ki set ek hi naam-type ka hai (andar check nahi)
Eviction insertion order se hai, read se order nahi badalta (LRU nahi)
common_mistakes: Map.set se refresh karke sochna ki entry end par gayi
Positive insert par negative entries na hatana
Store se pehle copy na karna
follow_up_questions: Agar rrs mein do alag types aa jaayein toh kya hoga?
delete + set ka cost kya hai, aur LRU ke liye getRRset mein kya badalna padega?

question: How does the cache bound its memory, why is eviction 'oldest inserted first' rather than LRU, and what are the weaknesses of that choice?
answer_hinglish:
Memory ek count se bound hai: maxEntries (default 10000), positive aur negative dono Maps ka total. Har putRRset aur putNegative ke baad evict() chalta hai: jab tak size > maxEntries, jo Map bada hai (barabar ho toh positive) uski pehli key delete. JS Map insertion order mein iterate karta hai, aur putRRset/putNegative refresh par delete + set karte hain, toh pehli key = sabse purani likhi hui entry. Har eviction O(1).

LRU kyun nahi? LRU ke liye har read par entry ko end par le jaana padta (delete + set in getRRset), jo bhi seedha hai -- lekin project ka scope correctness tha, aur README isse honestly 'NOT implemented' list mein rakhta hai: eviction 'oldest first' by insertion, not LRU. Test 'when full, the oldest entry is evicted' (maxEntries 3, 5 inserts, h0 gaya, h4 hai) yahi behaviour pin karta hai.

Kamzoriyan: (1) Ek popular naam jo 1 din ke TTL ke saath pehle cache hua, woh hazaaron one-off naamon ke baad evict ho jaata hai, chahe har second padha ja raha ho -- hit rate girta hai. (2) Expired entries ko prefer karke nahi nikaala jaata; lazy expiry ki wajah se woh slot gherti hain jab tak padhi na jaayein. (3) Limit entries mein hai, bytes mein nahi: ek bada TXT set aur ek A record barabar gine jaate hain. (4) Random naamon ki baarish (jaise Kaminsky style x1.bank.test, x2...) negative entries se cache bhar ke useful data evict kar sakti hai.

Koi performance number measure nahi kiya gaya; yeh reasoning hai, benchmark nahi.
why_needed: Bina bound ke ek long-running resolver attacker ke random naamon se ya natural growth se memory khatam kar dega.
real_world_analogy: Parking lot jahan jagah bharte hi sabse pehle aayi gaadi bahar -- chahe uska malik roz aata ho. LRU wala lot dekhta ki kaunsi gaadi sabse der se use nahi hui.
how_it_works: evict(): while size > maxEntries -> map = bigger of positive/negative -> map.keys().next() -> delete. Order = insertion order, refresh par delete+set.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts evict aur CacheOptions.maxEntries. README 'NOT implemented yet': 'Cache: eviction is "oldest first" by insertion, not LRU; no serve-stale (RFC 8767); no prefetch.'
advantages: O(1) eviction, koi extra data structure nahi
Memory hamesha bounded
Behaviour simple aur tested
disadvantages: Hot entries bhi evict ho jaati hain
Expired entries pehle nahi nikalti
Count-based, byte-based nahi
common_mistakes: Map.set se refresh karna (order nahi badalta, eviction galat entry nikaalegi)
Eviction sirf positive Map par lagana
maxEntries ko memory guarantee samajhna
follow_up_questions: LRU ke liye kya badlega aur uska cost kya hai?
Negative entries ko alag quota dena kyun accha ho sakta hai?
Bytes se limit kaise lagaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Insertion-order eviction simple aur O(1) hai; LRU bhi O(1) hai par har read ek write ban jaata hai. Byte accounting accurate hai par har RRset ka size nikaalna padega.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Random-subdomain flood se negative Map bhar jaata hai; 'bigger map first' rule positive data ko kuch had tak bachata hai lekin guarantee nahi.
advanced.alternatives: LRU (read par delete+set), LFU, 2Q/ARC jaise scan-resistant algorithms, alag positive/negative quotas, TTL-aware eviction (pehle expired).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x unique naamon par 10000 entries kam padengi; limit bytes mein, sharded caches (Unbound ke msg-cache aur rrset-cache slabs jaise) aur multi-thread access chahiye. Yahan kuch measure nahi kiya.
advanced.production_improvements: Eviction aur hit/miss counters export karna, maxEntries env se, expired-first sweep, aur LRU -- sab NOT implemented, README mein listed.

question: Why does the cache copy records both when storing and when returning them, and why does copyData treat TXT and RAW specially?
answer_hinglish:
Cache apne data ka akela maalik rehna chahiye. JavaScript mein objects reference se jaate hain: agar putRRset caller ka array/record seedha rakh le, ya getRRset internal object lauta de, toh caller ka koi bhi mutation (jaise resolver TTL badal de, ya server answer modify kare) cache ke andar ke data ko chupchaap badal dega -- aur woh agle client ko galat milega.

Isliye dono taraf copy: putRRset mein rrs.map((r) => ({ ...r, data: copyData(r.data) })), aur getRRset mein har record ka naya object with naya ttl aur copyData. getNegative bhi SOA ki copy deta hai. Read par copy waise bhi chahiye thi, kyunki har read ka TTL alag hota hai (countdown).

copyData special kyun? Spread ({ ...d }) sirf ek level deep copy karta hai. A, NS, CNAME, SOA, MX ke data mein sirf strings aur numbers hain -- woh immutable hain, shallow copy kaafi. TXT ke data mein texts: string[] hai -- array reference hai, isliye [...d.texts]. RAW (unknown types, RFC 3597) mein bytes: Buffer hai -- Buffer mutable hai, toh Buffer.from(d.bytes) se naya buffer.

Test 'returned records are copies: changing them does not change the cache': A record ka address bahar se 203.0.113.1 kar diya, phir dobara padha -- 192.0.2.1 hi mila.
why_needed: Shared mutable state cache bugs ka sabse chupa hua source hai; ek caller ki galti saare clients ko lag jaati hai.
real_world_analogy: Library photocopy deti hai, original kitaab nahi; aap photocopy par kuch bhi likho, agle reader ko saaf kitaab milti hai.
how_it_works: store: {...r, data: copyData(r.data)}. read: {...r, ttl, data: copyData(r.data)}. copyData: TXT -> texts array copy; RAW -> Buffer.from; baaki -> {...d}.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts copyData function (file ke end mein), putRRset, getRRset, putNegative, getNegative. Test cache.test.ts 'returned records are copies: changing them does not change the cache'.
advantages: Cache ke andar ka data bahar ke code se safe
Har read ko apna TTL milta hai
Copy sasti hai (chhote objects)
disadvantages: Har read par allocation -- bahut high QPS par GC pressure
Naya RData kind aaye jisme array ho toh copyData update karna yaad rakhna padega
common_mistakes: Sirf { ...r } karna aur nested array/Buffer share karna
Sirf read par copy karna, store par nahi
structuredClone har jagah lagana bina soche (Buffer ke saath behaviour aur cost)
follow_up_questions: Object.freeze se yahi guarantee kaise milti, aur kya kami rehti?
Naya RData type (jaise SVCB) add karne par copyData mein kya dekhoge?

question: Why does the cache take an injected clock (now) instead of calling Date.now() directly or tests using sleeps or fake timers?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki cache ke saare important rules time par depend karte hain -- TTL countdown, expiry, negative entry ki umar -- aur un rules ko test karne ke liye time ko control karna padta hai. CacheOptions.now ek function hai (default Date.now). Production mein kuch nahi badalta; test mein clock() helper ek variable t rakhta hai aur advance(sec) se usse aage badhata hai.

Alternatives: (1) Sleep: 300 s TTL test karne ke liye 300 s rukna -- impossible; chhote TTL (1 s) ke saath bhi tests slow aur flaky (timer jitter). (2) Vitest/Jest fake timers: Date.now ko globally patch karte hain. Yeh kaam karta, lekin yeh global hai -- resolver tests mein real UDP sockets aur timeouts (queryUdp ka timer) bhi chal rahe hain; global fake time un network timers ko bhi rok dega aur test hang ho sakta hai. (3) Injected clock: sirf cache ka time fake hai, network ka time asli. Yahi chuna.

Isse exact boundary test ho paati hai: 'an answer is re-fetched after its TTL (300 s), but the zone cut (86400 s) is still used' mein 299 s par 0 queries, 1 aur second par 1 query -- aur fake network asli sockets par chal raha hai. Unit test mein 100 s ka set 99 s par zinda, 100 s par khatam -- off-by-one bugs yahin pakde jaate hain.

Keemat: ek extra constructor option, aur yeh yaad rakhna ki cache ke andar kabhi seedha Date.now() na likhein.
why_needed: Time-dependent logic ko deterministic aur fast test karna, bina network timers ko chhede.
real_world_analogy: Cooking show mein 'yeh raha 2 ghante baad ka cake' -- oven ka asli intezaar nahi, lekin gas ka flame (network) asli hai.
how_it_works: new Cache({ now: c.now }) -> cache sirf this.now() use karta hai. clock(start).advance(sec) -> t += sec*1000. Resolver ko yahi cache pass hota hai, network real.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts CacheOptions.now aur constructor (opts.now ?? Date.now). test/cache.test.ts clock() helper aur 'cache: with the resolver' block ka make(c), jo Resolver ko cache inject karta hai.
advantages: Tests fast aur deterministic
Network timers par koi asar nahi
Exact boundaries (299 vs 300 s) test hoti hain
disadvantages: Ek aur option aur discipline: andar Date.now() na likhna
Resolver ka apna time (timeouts) is clock se nahi chalta -- do clocks
common_mistakes: Global fake timers lagana jab real sockets bhi chal rahe hon
TTL test ke liye sleep karna
Clock ko seconds mein dena jab cache ms expect karta hai
follow_up_questions: Monotonic clock (performance.now) ya Date.now -- cache ke liye kaun sahi hai?
Resolver ke timeouts bhi injectable hone chahiye kya?

question: How does the resolver use the cache at each step of a lookup, and why can an answer expire while the zone cut keeps being used?
answer_hinglish:
Resolver cache ko teen jagah use karta hai. (1) resolveOne ki shuruaat: getRRset(name, type, 'answer') -- seedha answer mila toh 0 queries. Phir getNegative(name, type) -- NXDOMAIN ya NODATA mila toh wahi. Phir (type CNAME nahi hai toh) cached CNAME -- mila toh caller target follow karta hai. (2) closestServers: naam se upar ki taraf chalta hai (www.alpha.test -> alpha.test -> test), har ancestor ka NS set getRRset(zone, NS, 'referral') se, aur NS hosts ke addresses cachedAddresses se. Jo sabse gehra zone mila jiske paas NS bhi hai aur kam se kam ek address bhi, wahin se shuru; kuch nahi toh root hints. (3) classify: har response ka bailiwick-filtered data likhta hai -- answers 'answer' rank par, referral ke NS aur glue 'referral' rank par, negatives putNegative se.

Answer aur zone cut alag RRsets hain alag TTL ke saath. Fixture mein www.alpha.test ka A 300 s ka hai, lekin test zone ne alpha.test ka NS set aur glue 86400 s ke saath diya. Toh 300 s baad sirf answer jaata hai; agla lookup closestServers se seedha alpha.test ke server par jaata hai -- 1 query, root nahi. Test: 'an answer is re-fetched after its TTL (300 s), but the zone cut (86400 s) is still used' (ALPHA1_IP log 1, ROOT_IP log 0).

Real internet par bhi yahi hota hai: TLD delegations ke TTL typically 1-2 din hote hain, website records minutes ke. Isi wajah se ek garm resolver kabhi kabhi hi root se baat karta hai. README ka live trace dikhata hai: 'org NS is cached, root skipped'.
why_needed: Cache sirf answers ke liye nahi, resolution ka raasta chhota karne ke liye bhi hai -- yahi recursive resolver ko fast banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Delhi se kisi mohalle ka ghar dhoondhna: pehli baar city -> area -> gali poochi. Ghar ka maalik badal gaya (answer expire), lekin gali ka raasta yaad hai, toh seedha gali mein jaakar poochte ho.
how_it_works: resolveOne: answer? -> negative? -> CNAME? -> closestServers(name) -> askZone loop -> classify -> cache writes -> referral toh serversFor aur loop.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts resolveOne, closestServers, cachedAddresses, classify, cacheAnswers. Resolver constructor mein opts.cache ?? new Cache(), aur Resolver.cache readonly public hai, tests usse inspect karte hain.
advantages: Garm cache par root aur TLD queries bahut kam
Answer aur delegation apne-apne TTL se jeete hain
Cache aur resolver ka interface chhota (4 methods)
disadvantages: NS set cached hai par saare addresses expire ho gaye toh zone cut skip hota hai, upar se shuru
Cached zone cut ke servers dead hon toh bhi pehle wahi try hote hain (RTT memory nahi)
common_mistakes: Sirf final answer cache karna, NS/glue nahi
closestServers mein NS mile par address check na karna
Referral data ko answer lookup mein use karna
follow_up_questions: Cached CNAME ka target alag zone mein ho toh kya hota hai?
Parent aur child ke NS TTL alag hon toh kiska use hona chahiye?

question: How can a recursive resolver be tested without the internet? Describe the fake network in test/fakenet.ts and test/fixtures.ts.
answer_hinglish:
Resolver ka kaam hi internet ke servers se baat karna hai, lekin tests ko internet par depend nahi karna chahiye: real servers badalte hain, network slow ya blocked ho sakta hai, aur misbehaviour (timeout, garbage, spoofing) real servers se karwa nahi sakte. Isliye project ne apna chhota 'internet' banaya.

test/fakenet.ts mein FakeServer hai: ek in-process authoritative DNS server, 127.0.0.1 ke ek ephemeral port par UDP aur TCP dono. Usko zones diye jaate hain (Zone { origin, records }), aur FakeServer.answer real authoritative logic chalata hai: zone cut ho toh referral (NS + glue), naam-type match ho toh answer, CNAME ho toh zone ke andar chase, warna NODATA ya NXDOMAIN with SOA, aur koi zone match na kare toh REFUSED. FakeNet in servers ko IP se rakhta hai aur route(ip) deta hai.

test/fixtures.ts ka buildNet() poora tree banata hai: root (198.51.100.1), test TLD, example TLD, alpha.test (do servers, in-bailiwick glue), beta.test (NS ns.hoster.example, bina glue), loop1/loop2.test (delegation loop), lame.test. FAKE_ROOT_HINTS mein sirf ek root hai. Saare addresses documentation ranges ke hain (192.0.2.x, 198.51.100.x, 203.0.113.x).

Resolver ko route: fake.route diya jaata hai, toh woh 'glue mein 192.0.2.1 mila' sochta hai aur packet asli loopback socket par jaata hai. Har server ka log hai, isliye tests gin sakte hain ki kaunse server ko kitni queries gayi. npm test: 80 tests, internet ki zaroorat nahi.
why_needed: Fast, repeatable tests jo failure cases bhi chala sakein -- real internet par yeh possible nahi.
real_world_analogy: Flight simulator: pilot asli cockpit buttons dabata hai (real sockets, real packets), lekin aasman aur mausam software ka hai -- aur engine fail bhi simulate kar sakte ho.
how_it_works: buildNet() -> FakeNet.add(ip, zones) per server -> start() har server ko UDP+TCP port deta hai -> Resolver({ rootHints: FAKE_ROOT_HINTS, route: fake.route }) -> queries loopback par -> FakeServer.answer -> log.
in_this_project: test/fakenet.ts (FakeServer, FakeNet, rr/A/NS/CNAME/SOA helpers, UDP_LIMIT 512, DEAD_PORT 9) aur test/fixtures.ts (buildNet, IP constants, BIG_TXT). resolver, cache aur server tests sab isi ko use karte hain.

Real sockets aur real wire format -- mock nahi
Har server ki query log assertion ke liye
disadvantages: Fake server ka logic real authoritative servers ke saare quirks nahi copy karta
Fixture tree ko samajhne mein pehle time lagta hai
common_mistakes: Transport ko mock kar dena (tab wire format aur sockets test hi nahi hote)
Tests mein real public IPs use karna
Ek hi fake server se saare zones serve karna (referrals test nahi honge)

Kaunsa bug fake network kabhi nahi pakad sakta?

question: How does FakeServer.answer decide between a referral, an answer, a CNAME, NODATA, NXDOMAIN and REFUSED, and how does it model UDP truncation?
answer_hinglish:
FakeServer.answer ek chhota authoritative server hai. Order: (1) Zone choose: is server ke zones mein se woh jiske neeche query ka naam hai, sabse lamba origin (most specific). Koi nahi toh REFUSED -- jaise real server jo zone serve nahi karta. (2) Delegation: zone ke records mein koi NS jo apex ka nahi hai aur query ka naam uske neeche hai -> referral: AA=0, authority mein woh NS set, additional mein un NS hosts ke A/AAAA (glue). (3) AA=1 set, phir exact naam-type match -> answer. (4) Naam par CNAME -> CNAME answer mein, aur target agar isi zone mein hai toh 8 baar tak chase karke target ke records bhi saath (jaise real servers karte hain). (5) Kuch nahi: agar koi bhi record is naam par ya iske neeche hai (isSubdomain(r.name, q.name)) toh NODATA -- isme empty non-terminal bhi aata hai (sub.alpha.test, kyunki host.sub.alpha.test exist karta hai); warna NXDOMAIN. Dono mein authority mein zone ka SOA.

Truncation handle() mein hai, answer() mein nahi: reply encode karke agar transport udp hai aur wire > UDP_LIMIT (512 bytes, RFC 1035 4.2.1) toh tc=true aur answer/authority/additional khaali. BIG_TXT (30 strings, lagbhag 930 bytes) isse trigger karta hai, aur resolver test 'a truncated (TC) UDP reply is retried over TCP to the same server' dikhata hai ki log mein ek udp aur ek tcp entry hai.

Hook truncation ke baad chalta hai, toh test chahe toh truncated reply bhi badal sakta hai.
why_needed: Resolver ke har outcome branch ko test karne ke liye server ko har tarah ka response dena aana chahiye -- sahi aur galat dono.
real_world_analogy: Post office ka counter: 'yeh area hamara nahi' (REFUSED), 'yeh area us branch ka hai, yeh raha unka address' (referral), 'yeh raha aapka letter' (answer), 'yeh insaan shift ho gaya, naya address yeh' (CNAME), 'ghar hai par is naam ka parcel nahi' (NODATA), 'is naam ka ghar hi nahi' (NXDOMAIN).
how_it_works: handle: decode -> log -> answer(query) -> encode -> udp && >512 ? TC + empty : wire -> hook? -> send. answer: zone -> cut? referral : match? answer : cname? chase : exists? NODATA : NXDOMAIN.
in_this_project: test/fakenet.ts FakeServer.answer aur handle; UDP_LIMIT constant. Fixtures: alpha.test mein chain c1..c10, loopa/loopb, dangling.alpha.test, host.sub.alpha.test (empty non-terminal ke liye).
advantages: Real authoritative behaviour ke main branches cover
Truncation asli size se trigger, flag se nahi
Same code se sahi aur hook se galat dono responses
disadvantages: Wildcards, DNAME, multiple-label delegation edge cases nahi
Same wire.ts encoder use karta hai jo test ho raha hai -- encoder ka bug dono taraf same ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Empty non-terminal ko NXDOMAIN bana dena
Referral mein AA=1 set karna
Truncation ko answer() ke andar karna jisse TCP par bhi truncate ho
follow_up_questions: Fake server aur resolver dono ek hi encoder use karte hain -- yeh risk kaise cover hua (interop test, live test)?
Wildcard support fake server mein kaise jodoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fake server simple rakha gaya taaki uske bugs resolver ke bugs na lagein; keemat yeh ki real-world quirks (wildcards, DNAME, broken glue) cover nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar fake server khud galat ho (jaise NODATA ki jagah NXDOMAIN), toh resolver ke tests galat behaviour ko sahi maan lenge -- isliye live test aur nslookup interop independent checks hain.
advanced.alternatives: Real authoritative server (NSD, Knot, BIND) Docker mein chalana; recorded pcap replay; pure mocks (sockets ke bina).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Test suite 10x badhe toh har describe mein buildNet aur start ka cost (har server do sockets) badhega; shared net aur reset() pehle se isi liye hain. Kuch measure nahi kiya.
advanced.production_improvements: Wildcard aur DNAME fixtures jodna jab resolver unhe support kare (abhi NOT implemented), aur ek real authoritative server ke against optional suite.

question: Why does the resolver take a route option that maps an IP to an endpoint, and why do the fixtures use documentation address ranges?
answer_hinglish:
Real DNS mein referral ka glue sirf IP deta hai -- 'ns1.alpha.test is 192.0.2.1' -- port kabhi nahi, kyunki port hamesha 53 hai. Test mein hum hazaar fake servers ko port 53 par nahi chala sakte (ek machine, ek 127.0.0.1, admin rights). Toh do raaste the: fixture zones mein loopback addresses aur custom ports ghusa do (zones real jaise nahi dikhenge, aur resolver ka 'port 53' logic badalna padega), ya resolver ke beech ek chhota 'routing table' daal do. Project ne doosra chuna.

ResolverOptions.route?: (ip) => Endpoint. Production default: (ip) => ({ host: ip, port: 53 }) -- identity. Tests mein FakeNet.route: IP se FakeServer dhoondho aur { host: '127.0.0.1', port: s.port } lautao. Resolver ka exchange() har query se pehle this.route(s.ip) karta hai, aur wahi Endpoint UDP aur TCP retry dono ke liye use hota hai. Unknown IP ko DEAD_PORT (9) milta hai -- ek 'dead host' jo timeout ya refusal deta hai, all-dead aur timeout tests ke liye.

Documentation ranges kyun? 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24 (RFC 5737) internet par kabhi route nahi hote. Agar route mein bug ho aur packet bahar nikal jaaye, toh woh kisi asli server tak nahi pahunchega. Aur zones bilkul real zones jaise dikhte hain, toh resolver ka code test aur production mein same hai -- sirf ek function badla.

Yeh dependency injection ka hi pattern hai: network ka sirf 'address resolution' hissa inject hota hai, poora transport nahi -- sockets, timeouts, spoofing checks asli chalte hain.
why_needed: Real-looking zones aur real sockets ke saath tests chalane ke liye IP aur actual socket address ke beech ek seam chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Courier company ka sorting centre: parcel par asli pincode likha hai (IP), lekin training warehouse mein har pincode ek shelf number (loopback port) par map hota hai. Delivery boy ka process same rehta hai.
how_it_works: glue IP -> Server { ip } -> exchange: to = route(ip) -> queryUdp(to) / queryTcp(to). FakeNet.route: servers.get(ip) ? { 127.0.0.1, s.port } : { 127.0.0.1, DEAD_PORT }.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts constructor (this.route = opts.route ?? ((ip) => ({ host: ip, port: 53 }))) aur exchange. test/fakenet.ts FakeNet.route aur DEAD_PORT. test/fixtures.ts ke IP constants (ROOT_IP 198.51.100.1, ALPHA1_IP 192.0.2.1, HOSTER_IP 203.0.113.5).
advantages: Production aur test mein resolver ka code same
Fixtures real zones jaise
Bug hone par bhi packet internet par kisi ke paas nahi jaata
disadvantages: Ek production option jo sirf tests ke liye hai (galat config par traffic galat jagah ja sakta hai)
Route hook ke bina port 53 ke alawa kuch test nahi hota
common_mistakes: Fixtures mein real public IPs use karna
Poora transport mock karna (spoofing checks untested reh jaate)
UDP aur TCP ke liye alag route dena (TC retry 'same server' ka matlab tootega)
follow_up_questions: Route hook ko production mein kisi kaam ke liye use kar sakte ho (jaise forwarding)?

question: Why must each fake server listen on UDP and TCP on the same port, and how does FakeServer.start get such a port reliably?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki resolver ka TCP fallback 'usi server' se poochta hai: exchange() mein ek hi Endpoint (to = route(ip)) hai; UDP reply TC=1 aaye toh queryTcp(to, ...) usi host aur port par TCP connect karta hai. Real DNS mein yeh natural hai -- port 53 UDP aur TCP dono. Agar fake server ka TCP alag port par hota, toh route ko do ports lautane padte aur resolver ka production code test ke liye badalna padta.

Problem: OS se 'koi bhi free port' (bind 0) maangne par UDP ka port milta hai; TCP ka namespace alag hai, aur same number par TCP koi aur process (ya parallel test worker) pehle se use kar raha ho sakta hai. Yeh ek race hai jo machine aur timing par depend karti hai.

FakeServer.start ka hal: loop mein 20 attempts tak -- UDP ko 127.0.0.1:0 par bind karo, port padho, usi port par TCP listen karo. TCP 'error' event (EADDRINUSE) aaye toh UDP socket band karo aur naya port try karo. Success par dono rakh lo. 20 baar bhi na mile toh clear error: 'could not get the same UDP and TCP port'. Yeh check-then-act race ko retry se handle karta hai, assume nahi karta ki port free hoga.

Concurrency ka doosra hissa: FakeServer.onTcp ek LengthPrefixedReader se frames nikalta hai (2-byte length prefix), toh ek TCP chunk mein do queries ya aadhi query bhi sahi handle hoti hai; stop() saare open TCP sockets destroy karta hai taaki test process latke nahi.
why_needed: TC -> TCP retry ka test tabhi meaningful hai jab TCP usi endpoint par ho jahan UDP gaya tha -- bilkul real DNS ki tarah.
real_world_analogy: Ek dukaan jiska counter (UDP) aur godown ka darwaza (TCP) same address par hona chahiye; agar godown ka number kisi aur ne le liya hai toh dukaan doosri gali mein shift karo, tab tak jab dono number free mile.
how_it_works: for attempt < 20: udp.bind(0) -> port -> tcp.listen(port) -> error? udp.close, continue : save, return. throw after 20.
in_this_project: test/fakenet.ts FakeServer.start, onTcp, stop. src/transport.ts LengthPrefixedReader aur frameTcp jo fake server bhi reuse karta hai. src/resolver.ts exchange (same `to` for UDP and TCP).

Port race retry se handle, flaky failure nahi
Clear error message agar sach mein port na mile
disadvantages: 20 attempts ek arbitrary limit hai
Har server do sockets leta hai; bahut bade fixture par file descriptors
common_mistakes: Maan lena ki UDP ka free port TCP mein bhi free hoga
Fixed ports (jaise 5300) tests mein hardcode karna -- parallel runs mein clash
stop() mein open TCP connections destroy na karna (process hang)
follow_up_questions: Parallel test workers ke saath yeh race kitni common hai?

question: How do the FakeServer hooks and query logs let tests simulate misbehaving servers and attackers? Give examples from the tests.
answer_hinglish:
Har FakeServer par ek optional hook hai, type Hook = (ctx: HookCtx) => Message | Buffer | 'drop' | undefined (ya Promise). handle() pehle normal reply banata hai, phir hook ko HookCtx deta hai: query (decoded), reply (jo bhejne wala tha), transport, send (isi server ke socket se extra raw bytes bhejo) aur spoof (ek DOOSRE port se bytes bhejo -- off-path attacker). Return value decide karta hai: 'drop' toh kuch mat bhejo (timeout simulate), Buffer toh woh raw bytes (garbage), Message toh woh message, undefined toh normal reply.

Examples: timeout ke liye hook 'drop' lautata hai aur test dekhta hai ki next server try hua. 'a reply from a different source port (off-path spoofer with the right ID) is ignored' mein hook spoof() se 203.0.113.66 wala fake answer bhejta hai, phir undefined lauta kar asli reply jaane deta hai; resolver ka answer asli addresses hain aur onIgnored ne 'wrong-source' report kiya. 'a reply that echoes a different question is ignored' mein send() se evil.alpha.test wala reply pehle bhejta hai -> 'mismatch'. Bailiwick tests reply mein doosre zone ke records ghusa kar dekhte hain ki cache mein nahi gaye.

Log: har decoded query ka QueryLogEntry { name, type, transport, id, rd, port } push hota hai. Isse assertions: RD=0 har query par, kaunse server ko kitni queries, udp ke baad tcp, aur 'query IDs and source ports are random'. reset() log aur hook dono saaf karta hai -- beforeEach mein chalta hai taaki ek test ka hook doosre mein leak na ho.
why_needed: Failure aur attack paths ko deterministic tarike se trigger karna, bina resolver ke code mein test-only branches daale.
real_world_analogy: Mock drill: building ka asli fire alarm system, lekin drill officer kisi ek floor par 'aag' ka signal (hook) daalta hai aur register (log) mein dekhta hai kaun kis raaste se nikla.
how_it_works: handle -> log.push -> reply -> hook?({query, reply, transport, send, spoof}) -> 'drop' | Buffer | Message | undefined -> send.
in_this_project: test/fakenet.ts: Hook, HookCtx, QueryLogEntry, FakeServer.reset, FakeNet.totalQueries. test/resolver.test.ts ka 'resolver: spoofing and cache-poisoning defences' block aur 'resolver: TCP fallback and failing servers' block.
advantages: Ek hook se timeout, garbage, spoof, poisoning sab
Resolver code mein koi test-only branch nahi
Log se exact query counts assert hote hain
disadvantages: Hook truncation ke baad chalta hai -- order samajhna padta hai
spoof sirf loopback par kaam karta hai; real off-path attacker ka network behaviour nahi
common_mistakes: beforeEach mein reset() bhoolna (hook agle test mein leak)
Spoof test mein asli reply bhi drop kar dena (tab test sirf timeout dikhata hai)
Log ki jagah resolver ke internal state par assert karna
follow_up_questions: onIgnored callback resolver mein kyun hai -- sirf tests ke liye?
Ek hook se Kaminsky jaisa race kaise simulate karoge?

question: What does the opt-in live test (test/live.test.ts) check against the real internet, why is it opt-in, and what was the result?
answer_hinglish:
Fake network ke tests saabit karte hain ki resolver hamare fixtures ke saath sahi hai. Lekin fixtures humne khud likhe, aur fake server bhi hamara hi encoder use karta hai -- toh ek independent check chahiye ki asli internet par bhi kaam karta hai. Woh hai test/live.test.ts, jo sirf LIVE_DNS=1 par chalta hai (describe.skipIf(!live)).

Kya check hota hai: (1) a.root-servers.net ka A aur AAAA -- hamare root-hints.ts wale addresses (198.41.0.4, 2001:503:ba3e::2:30) se match, aur A OS resolver se bhi match. (2) example.com A non-empty aur OS resolver jaisa hi set. (3) www.wikipedia.org par CNAME chain follow hoti hai aur A milte hain. (4) gmail.com MX c-ares (node:dns Resolver) se match -- sirf LIVE_DNS_CHECK_SERVER set ho tab. (5) does-not-exist.invalid seedha root se NXDOMAIN with SOA. (6) pehle lookup ka trace print (README ke liye).

Opt-in kyun: isko outbound UDP/TCP port 53 chahiye; bahut corporate/cloud networks isse block karte hain, aur real internet slow ya badalta hua hai -- default npm test ko internet par depend nahi karna chahiye. Har test ka timeout 30 s hai.

Result (README, 2026-11-21, ek baar): LIVE_DNS_CHECK_SERVER ke saath 6 of 6 passed; uske bina 5 passed + 1 skipped. Bonus finding: gmail.com MX trace mein Google ke server ne 10 *.l.google.com address records bheje jo bailiwick rule ne drop kar diye -- real data par rule kaam karta dikha.
why_needed: Apne hi fixtures ke against pass hona aur asli duniya mein kaam karna alag cheezein hain; ek independent check zaroori hai.
real_world_analogy: Car ko factory test track par chalana (fake net) aur phir ek baar asli highway par (live test) -- har roz highway par nahi jaate, lekin release se pehle zaroor.
how_it_works: LIVE_DNS=1 -> new Resolver({ timeoutMs: 3000, trace }) with real ROOT_HINTS aur identity route -> real roots -> answers compare with dns.lookup / c-ares.
in_this_project: test/live.test.ts: live, checkServer, osLookup4, addrs helpers; README section 'Live test against the real root servers (opt-in LIVE_DNS=1)'.

Real root hints ka sanity check

Real answers ko hardcode karna (example.com ke IPs badal sakte hain)

question: The live cross-check with node:dns failed with ECONNREFUSED on the development machine. How was that investigated and fixed?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: live test mein hamara resolver sahi answer de raha tha, lekin comparison wala hissa -- node:dns ka Resolver (c-ares library) -- ECONNREFUSED de raha tha. Matlab bug hamare code mein nahi, oracle (comparison tool) mein tha.

Investigation: pehle dekho ki kaunsa call fail ho raha hai -- hamara resolve() ya cares.resolveMx(). Phir dekho c-ares kis server se baat kar raha hai (Resolver ka getServers() yahi batata hai). README ka finding: is machine par c-ares ne 127.0.0.1 ko apna DNS server chuna, aur wahan koi DNS server nahi sun raha tha, isliye connection refused. Isi machine par OS ka apna resolver (getaddrinfo) theek kaam kar raha tha -- toh c-ares aur OS alag-alag jagah se config padh rahe the.

Fix (do hisse): (1) A records ke liye oracle badla -- dns.lookup(name, { all: true, family: 4 }) jo OS ka getaddrinfo use karta hai; yeh kisi bhi working-DNS machine par kaam karta hai. osLookup4 helper yahi hai. (2) c-ares wale checks (gmail.com MX, aur .invalid ka ENOTFOUND) sirf tab chalte hain jab LIVE_DNS_CHECK_SERVER=<ip> diya ho; tab cares.setServers([checkServer]) explicit server set karta hai. Bina variable ke MX test it.skipIf se skip hota hai.

Result: variable ke saath 6/6, bina 5 + 1 skipped. Lesson: jab test kisi doosre system ko oracle bana raha ho, toh oracle ka failure apne code ka failure na samjho -- pehle alag karo kaun fail hua. PLAN.md ke 'Decisions changed' section mein yeh likha hua hai.
why_needed: Galat diagnosis se log apna sahi code 'fix' karne lagte hain; oracle aur subject ko alag karna debugging ka pehla step hai.
real_world_analogy: Weighing scale se apna wazan check kar rahe ho aur reading error aa rahi hai -- problem aapke wazan mein nahi, scale ki battery mein hai. Doosra scale use karo, ya battery daal kar hi us scale par bharosa karo.
how_it_works: cares = new dns.Resolver(); checkServer ? cares.setServers([checkServer]) : default (here 127.0.0.1 -> ECONNREFUSED). A checks -> dns.lookup (getaddrinfo). MX -> it.skipIf(!checkServer).
in_this_project: test/live.test.ts header comment, checkServer, cares, osLookup4, aur 'MX of gmail.com matches node:dns (needs LIVE_DNS_CHECK_SERVER)'. PLAN.md: 'Live cross-check uses the OS resolver, not c-ares, by default.'
advantages: A record check har machine par chalta hai
c-ares check explicit server ke saath reliable
Skip clearly report hota hai, chupchaap pass nahi
disadvantages: Bina variable ke MX aur NXDOMAIN ka cross-check nahi hota
dns.lookup sirf addresses deta hai, MX nahi
common_mistakes: Oracle ke error ko apne resolver ka bug samajhna
c-ares failure ko try/catch se chupa kar test pass karwa dena
Hardcoded public resolver IP test mein daal dena
follow_up_questions: dns.lookup aur dns.resolve4 mein kya fark hai (getaddrinfo vs c-ares)?
c-ares ne 127.0.0.1 kyun chuna hoga -- kaise confirm karoge?

question: A mutation check removed the per-resolution query budget and no test failed. How do you find out why, and what was the fix?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: mutation R8 (no per-resolution query budget) ke baad poora suite green raha. Matlab ya toh limit bekaar hai, ya koi test usse alag se check nahi karta. Debugging ka sawaal: kaunsa test is limit ko exercise karta tha, aur woh kyun nahi gira?

Investigation: jo test budget ke baare mein hai woh dhoondho -- 'a delegation loop without glue (loop1.test <-> loop2.test) ends in SERVFAIL, within the budget'. Uska assert padho: rcode SERVFAIL, queries <= 40, aur reason regex /deeper than|budget|no address/ -- yani test kisi bhi limit ka reason accept karta hai. Loop ko do limits rok sakti hain: query budget (maxQueries) aur NS-lookup nesting limit (maxDepth, default 4). Ek hata do toh doosri wahi SERVFAIL de deti hai, aur regex phir bhi match karta hai. Mutation R9 (no nesting limit) bhi isi wajah se bacha. Ek test, do guards, koi bhi akela untested. (Mutant ke saath Resolver ka trace option ya r.reason print karke dekh sakte ho ki kaunsi limit lagi.)

Fix: har guard ka apna test jo DOOSRE guard ke bina fail ho. 'the query budget alone: maxQueries 2 cannot finish a 3-query lookup' (normal root -> test -> alpha.test 3 queries hai) aur 'the nesting limit alone: maxDepth 0 forbids the nested NS lookup that beta.test needs'. Re-run par R8 aur R9 dono exactly naye test se pakde gaye.

Same pattern W3 mein tha: 'half a pointer' test WireError toh deta tha, lekin baad ke check (question type field) se, pointer guard se nahi. Fix: readName ko seedha [0, 0xc0] par call karna. General lesson: 'error aaya' assert karna kaafi nahi; jab ek se zyada defences hon, har ek ko akela test karo.
why_needed: Jo safety limit kabhi akela test nahi hua, woh refactor mein chupchaap toot sakta hai aur koi nahi jaanega.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ke darwaze par do taale hain. Aap test karte ho 'darwaza khulta nahi' -- pass. Lekin ek taala toota ho toh bhi pass hoga. Har taale ko alag se check karna padta hai.
how_it_works: mutant -> suite green -> related test dhoondho -> trace se actual failure reason -> doosra guard mil gaya -> har guard ke liye isolated test (doosre ko loose karke).
in_this_project: README 'Mutation checks' table: R8 aur R9 '0 (not caught) -> 1 with the new test'. test/resolver.test.ts mein dono naye tests. src/resolver.ts askZone (budget) aur serversFor (maxDepth).
advantages: Masked guards pakde gaye
Naye tests chhote aur specific
Trace se reason dikhta hai, guess nahi
disadvantages: Mutation testing haath se ki gayi, har check ek manual text replacement
Loop test ka reason regex ab bhi dono guards ko accept karta hai, toh woh akela kisi ek guard ko protect nahi karta
common_mistakes: Reason ko itne dheele regex se match karna ki koi bhi guard chalega
Do guards ko ek hi test se cover maan lena
Mutant bach gaya toh guard hi hata dena ('kaam ka nahi')
follow_up_questions: Loop test ka regex /deeper than|budget|no address/ dheela kyun rakha gaya -- kya yeh sahi choice hai?
Equivalent mutant aur masked mutant mein kya fark hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Do overlapping guards defence-in-depth dete hain; keemat yeh ki tests ko har ek ko alag se isolate karna padta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina isolated test ke koi refactor budget check hata de toh delegation-loop test phir bhi pass hoga, aur ek aisa input jahan depth limit na lage (jaise bahut saare NS hosts) budget ke bina bahut queries bhejega.
advanced.alternatives: Stryker jaisa automated mutation tool; har guard ka alag reason assert karna (naye tests yahi karte hain: /budget of 2/, /deeper than 0/); property-based tests.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade codebase mein manual mutation (41 checks) scale nahi karta; automated tool aur CI mein incremental mutation chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Mutation run ko script banana taaki har release par chale, aur har naye guard ke saath uska isolated test likhna.

question: What is mutation testing as it was done in this project, what did the cache checks C1-C10 show, and what is an equivalent mutant?
answer_hinglish:
Mutation testing tests ko test karta hai. Code coverage batata hai ki line chali; mutation batata hai ki agar line galat ho jaaye toh koi test girega ya nahi. Is project mein yeh haath se kiya gaya: src/ mein ek exact text replacement se ek rule toda, poora suite chalaya, phir file restore ki (git status clean). Check 'pass' tab hai jab kam se kam ek test red ho.

41 checks the (W wire, T transport, R resolver, C cache, S server): 36 pehli baar mein pakde gaye, 5 nahi. Cache ke saare 10 pakde gaye: C1 entries never expire (3 tests), C2 TTL first record se (1), C3 SOA minimum ignore (2), C4 NXDOMAIN per type (2), C5 referral overwrites answer (1), C6 referral returned as answer (2), C7 TTL 0 cached (1), C8 no maxTtl (1), C9 negative never expire (2), C10 no-SOA negative cached (1). Jahan sirf 1 test pakadta hai, wahi test us rule ka akela guard hai -- usse kabhi delete mat karna.

Equivalent mutant: aisa badlaav jo program ka observable behaviour badalta hi nahi, toh koi behaviour test usse pakad hi nahi sakta. Project ka example W4: label bytes ka bounds check hatao, toh label chhota kat jaata hai, pos end ke paar jaata hai, aur loop ka agla check ('name runs past the end') wahi WireError phenk deta hai. Result same, sirf error message ki precision alag. README ise honestly equivalent mark karta hai; check rakha gaya kyunki sahi message deta hai.

Bache hue 4 (W3, W7, R8, R9) asli gaps the aur har ek ke liye naya test aaya; re-run par har ek exactly naye test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Green suite ka matlab yeh nahi ki rules protected hain; mutation testing batata hai kaunse rules sach mein tests se bandhe hain.
real_world_analogy: Security guard ko test karne ke liye manager khud nakli chor bhejta hai. Agar chor nikal gaya, toh guard ki training mein gap hai -- chahe guard roz duty par aata ho (coverage).
how_it_works: rule chuno -> ek text replace -> npm test -> red tests gino -> restore -> 0 hai toh: asli gap (naya test) ya equivalent (reason likho).
in_this_project: README.md 'Mutation checks (2026-11-21)' table aur uske neeche explanation. Cache checks ke guard tests test/cache.test.ts mein (jaise C2 ke liye 'an RRset lives for its smallest TTL, and reads count the TTL down').

# 1. in src/cache.ts replace
#      if (ttl <= 0) return false;
#    with
#      if (ttl < 0) return false;
# 2. npm test        -> 1 test red: 'TTL 0 is never cached; a huge TTL is capped at maxTtl'

Har rule ka guard test pata chalta hai

Mutant choice insaan ki samajh par depend -- jo rule socha hi nahi, woh test nahi hua

Bache mutant ke liye guard code hi hata dena
Equivalent mutant ke liye zabardasti test likhna jo implementation detail check kare
