question: A zone operator fixes a broken record, but users behind this resolver keep getting the old NXDOMAIN or the old address. Explain why and what limits the damage.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh caching ka seedha nateeja hai: resolver ne purana answer (ya 'nahi hai') TTL tak yaad rakha hai, aur TTL khatam hone tak woh upstream poochega hi nahi. Isme bug nahi, yeh contract hai -- lekin kitni der tak galat rahega, yeh cache ke rules decide karte hain.

Galat NXDOMAIN: putNegative TTL = min(SOA TTL, SOA minimum, maxNegativeTtl). Zone ka SOA minimum 1 din ho, tab bhi yahan cap 3 ghante (10800 s) hai -- RFC 2308 ka suggestion. Toh worst case 3 ghante. Aur agar beech mein koi us naam ka koi bhi positive record seekh le (jaise kisi aur type ka answer), toh putRRset us naam ka NX entry turant hata deta hai. Galat address: TTL zone ne diya tha, max 1 din (maxTtl 86400) cap. Owner ko change se pehle TTL kam karna chahiye tha -- standard practice.

Is project mein kya NAHI hai: koi admin command ya API nahi jisse ek entry flush karein. Cache.clear() method hai par sirf code se; server mein expose nahi. Practical fix process restart hai (memory cache, persistence nahi) -- ya TTL ka intezaar. Serve-stale (RFC 8767) bhi nahi hai, jo ulti problem solve karta hai (upstream down ho toh purana answer).

Doosra failure: cached zone cut ke servers badal gaye (NS migration). Hamara NS set referral rank par 86400 s tak reh sakta hai; agar purane servers band ho gaye, askZone har ek par timeout khata hai, phir 'all servers failed' -> SERVFAIL, aur cache khud se root par wapas nahi jaata jab tak NS ya unke addresses expire na ho jaayein. Real resolvers is case mein parent se dobara poochte hain; yahan implement nahi hai.
why_needed: Operators aur users ko samajhna chahiye ki DNS changes 'turant' kyun nahi dikhte, aur resolver ki taraf se damage kaun bound karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Newspaper ki galat khabar: subah chhap gayi toh shaam tak (TTL) logon ke paas wahi rahegi. Agle edition mein correction aayega. Editor ka rule hai ki koi bhi 'nahi mila' wali khabar 3 ghante se zyada nahi chhapegi.
how_it_works: Galat negative -> max min(SOA ttl, minimum, 3h); positive aane par NX delete. Galat positive -> max min(record ttls, 1 day). Flush -> sirf restart / clear() in code. Dead cached NS -> timeouts -> SERVFAIL until expiry.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts putNegative (maxNegativeTtl 10800), putRRset (maxTtl 86400 aur negative cleanup), clear(). src/resolver.ts closestServers (cached cut pehle) aur askZone. README 'NOT implemented yet': no serve-stale, no RTT/dead-server memory.
advantages: Negative cap galat NXDOMAIN ko 3 ghante tak bound karta hai
Positive answer purane negative ko turant hata deta hai
Restart = clean slate (persistence nahi)
disadvantages: Ek entry flush karne ka koi operational tarika nahi
Dead cached NS se lookups SERVFAIL ho sakte hain jab tak expiry
Restart poora warm cache bhi kho deta hai
common_mistakes: Sochna ki DNS change turant propagate hota hai
Negative TTL ka cap na lagana
Restart ko flush ka normal tarika banana production mein
follow_up_questions: Unbound mein 'flush' kaise hota hai (unbound-control flush)?
Cached NS ke saare servers dead hon toh resolver ko kya karna chahiye?
Serve-stale aur yeh failure ek doosre ke ulte kaise hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Lambe TTL kam upstream load dete hain par change slow dikhte hain; chhote TTL fast change par zyada load. Cache ka cap owner ke TTL ko override karta hai -- 1 din aur 3 ghante tradeoff points hain.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat NXDOMAIN 3 ghante; galat address 1 din tak; NS migration ke baad purane dead servers par timeouts aur SERVFAIL jab tak NS/glue expire.
advanced.alternatives: Admin flush API (per name/zone), lame/dead server memory ke saath parent se re-query, serve-stale (RFC 8767), chhote caps configurable.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare clients ek resolver ke peeche hon toh ek galat entry sab par lagti hai; multiple resolver instances ho toh flush har instance par karna padega (shared cache ka sawaal).
advanced.production_improvements: Control channel (local socket) se flush name/zone, metrics mein negative hits, NS ke failures par cut invalidate karna -- sab NOT implemented.

question: This resolver serves one machine on loopback. What would have to change to serve 10x or 100x more clients, and what would you measure first?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baat: is project mein koi load test ya timing measure nahi hui. README kehta hai 'No timings are claimed'. Toh yeh design reasoning hai, numbers nahi.

Abhi ka shape: ek Node process, ek event loop, ek Resolver aur ek in-memory Cache (Map, maxEntries 10000), DnsServer UDP aur TCP same port par, loopback only. Har upstream UDP query ke liye naya socket random port par (spoofing defence). Concurrent client queries event loop par interleave hoti hain; Map par koi lock nahi chahiye kyunki JS single-threaded hai.

10x par pehle kya tootega: (1) cache size -- 10000 entries aur insertion-order eviction se hit rate girega; bytes-based limit aur LRU chahiye. (2) In-flight dedupe nahi hai: ek popular naam expire hote hi saare concurrent clients alag-alag upstream jaate hain (thundering herd). (3) Dead server ki memory nahi: har lookup jo dead server pehle chune, poora timeout (2000 ms default) khata hai. (4) Per-query socket: file descriptors aur ephemeral ports ka load.

100x par: ek process kaafi nahi; multiple processes/threads (Node cluster ya SO_REUSEPORT) -- lekin tab har process ka alag cache hoga, hit rate batega; shared cache (sharded in-memory jaise Unbound, ya external store) ka design chahiye. Rate limiting aur access control (abhi sirf loopback guard), EDNS(0) taaki kam TCP fallback ho, prefetch taaki popular naam kabhi cold na hon.

Measure pehle: cache hit ratio, upstream queries per client query (Resolution.queries already hai), p50/p99 latency, timeouts per server, event loop lag, open sockets. Tool typically dnsperf/resperf jaisa load generator.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki aap prototype aur production ka fark jaante ho aur bottlenecks ko order mein soch sakte ho bina numbers ghade.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki rasoi se restaurant: ek chulha (event loop) aur ek fridge (cache) 4 logon ke liye theek; 400 ke liye zyada chulhe, bada aur organised fridge, aur ek hi dish ke 20 order aayein toh ek baar banao (dedupe).
how_it_works: client -> DnsServer.handle -> Resolver.resolve -> Cache -> (miss) upstream sockets. Scale points: cache size/eviction, dedupe, server selection, process model, shared cache, rate limits.
in_this_project: src/server.ts DnsServer (opts.resolver.resolve per query), src/resolver.ts Resolution.queries counter, src/cache.ts maxEntries/evict. README 'NOT implemented yet' list mein RTT selection, in-flight dedupe, LRU, prefetch, serve-stale, EDNS(0), rate limiting.
advantages: Clean layering (server / resolver / cache) se har hissa alag scale ho sakta hai
Resolution.queries pehle se ek useful metric hai
Single-threaded hone se cache mein lock ki zaroorat nahi
disadvantages: Ek process, ek cache, koi dedupe nahi
Koi metrics export nahi
Dead server har baar timeout
common_mistakes: Bina measure kiye numbers bolna
Pehle multi-process karna aur cache split hone ka asar bhoolna
Sirf CPU sochna jab bottleneck upstream latency aur timeouts hain
follow_up_questions: Multiple processes mein cache share kaise karoge -- aur kya karna bhi chahiye?
In-flight dedupe ka design kya hoga?
Kaunsa metric sabse pehle dashboard par chahiye?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Single process simple aur consistent cache deta hai; multi-process throughput deta hai par cache fragment hota hai. Shared external cache network hop jodta hai jo DNS ke liye mehenga hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Popular naam expire -> herd upstream; ek zone ke dead server se latency spike; random-name flood se cache churn; open resolver bane toh amplification.
advanced.alternatives: Unbound/BIND/PowerDNS Recursor jaisa production resolver use karna; forwarding mode (upstream recursive ko bhejna); anycast fleet with per-node cache.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: LRU + bytes limit, dedupe, RTT-based server selection. 100x: multi-core (threads/processes) with sharded cache, rate limiting, EDNS(0), prefetch, metrics. Is project mein in mein se kuch implement nahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Pehle metrics (hit ratio, upstream/query, timeouts, latency histogram), phir dedupe aur dead-server memory, phir multi-core -- har step measure karke.

question: What do production resolvers such as Unbound or BIND do that this resolver does not, and which of those would you add first?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: bahut kuch, aur README unme se zyada tar ko honestly 'NOT implemented yet' list mein rakhta hai. Main ones:

(1) RTT-based server selection: Unbound har server ka smoothed round-trip time aur timeouts yaad rakhta hai aur fast server ko prefer karta hai; dead server ko kuch der ke liye avoid. Yahan askZone har baar random order (shuffled) mein try karta hai, toh dead server har baar ek poora timeout khilata hai. (2) Prefetch: popular entry ka TTL khatam hone se pehle (typically aakhri 10 percent mein) background mein refresh, taaki users ko kabhi miss na dikhe. Yahan nahi. (3) Serve-stale (RFC 8767): upstream down ho toh expired answer thodi der aur do. Yahan nahi -- getRRset expired entry delete kar deta hai. (4) In-flight dedupe: ek naam ke concurrent misses ek hi upstream query share karein. Yahan nahi. (5) QNAME minimisation (RFC 9156): root ko sirf 'com' poocho, poora naam nahi -- privacy. Yahan har server poora naam dekhta hai. (6) EDNS(0): bade UDP replies aur DNSSEC ka base; yahan OPT kabhi nahi bheja jaata, 512 byte limit, zyada TCP fallback. (7) DNSSEC validation, 0x20, root priming, aggressive NSEC caching, rate limiting, access control lists.

Pehle kya? Main RTT/dead-server memory chunoonga, kyunki yeh user latency ka sabse bada aur sabse common source hai (ek dead server = poora timeout per lookup), aur yeh askZone mein localized change hai. Uske baad in-flight dedupe (load), phir EDNS(0) (kam TCP). Security ke liye asli fix DNSSEC hai, lekin woh sabse bada kaam hai.

Interview mein yeh kehna important hai ki yeh project learning ke liye hai; production mein main Unbound jaisa mature resolver chalata, khud ka nahi.
why_needed: Apne system ki limits jaanna aur unhe priority mein rakh paana senior engineer ka signal hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka bana scooter vs company ki car: dono chalte hain, lekin car mein ABS, airbags, GPS reroute (RTT selection), aur petrol khatam hone se pehle warning (prefetch) hai.
how_it_works: Missing: RTT selection, prefetch, serve-stale, in-flight dedupe, QNAME minimisation, EDNS(0), DNSSEC, 0x20, root priming. Order: RTT/dead memory -> dedupe -> EDNS -> DNSSEC.
in_this_project: README 'NOT implemented yet (honest list)'. src/resolver.ts askZone (shuffled order, koi RTT nahi), src/cache.ts getRRset (expired delete, no serve-stale), src/server.ts (EDNS OPT ignore).
advantages: Missing features ki list README mein honest hai
Code chhota hai toh har feature ki jagah saaf dikhti hai
Priority order reasoning ke saath
disadvantages: Production mein use karne layak nahi
Dead server, cold popular names, aur privacy -- teeno ka asar real users par
common_mistakes: Claim karna ki yeh production-ready hai
DNSSEC ko 'random ports ke baad zaroori nahi' samajhna
Sab features ek saath jodne ki koshish
follow_up_questions: RTT tracking ka data structure kaisa hoga aur kab bhoolna chahiye?
QNAME minimisation se kaun se broken servers toot jaate hain?
Serve-stale kab dangerous hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har feature complexity jodta hai: RTT selection mein state aur decay, prefetch mein background load, serve-stale mein galat data serve karne ka risk, QNAME minimisation mein broken servers ke workarounds.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina RTT memory: dead server se latency spike. Bina prefetch: popular naam ke expire par herd. Bina serve-stale: upstream outage = user outage. Bina dedupe: duplicate upstream load.
advanced.alternatives: Mature resolver (Unbound, BIND, Knot Resolver, PowerDNS Recursor) chalana; ya forwarding mode jisme ek trusted upstream recursive saara kaam kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x par yahi features luxury nahi, zaroorat ban jaate hain -- dedupe aur prefetch upstream load ko control karte hain, RTT selection tail latency ko.
advanced.production_improvements: Order: dead-server/RTT memory, in-flight dedupe, EDNS(0), metrics, phir serve-stale aur prefetch, aur lambi term mein DNSSEC -- sab abhi NOT implemented.

question: Exercise: change the cache's eviction from 'oldest inserted' to LRU (a read refreshes an entry's position) and write a test that proves the difference.
answer_hinglish:
Map insertion order ko hi LRU list ki tarah use kar sakte hain -- koi naya data structure nahi chahiye. Abhi putRRset delete + set karta hai taaki refresh hua entry end par jaaye; evict() Map ki pehli key nikaalta hai. LRU ke liye bas getRRset mein bhi, successful hit par (expiry aur rank check ke baad), same delete + set kar do. Tab pehli key = sabse der se use na hui entry.

Dhyan dene wali baatein: (1) Expired entry par position mat badlo, woh waise bhi delete hoti hai. (2) Rank check fail ho (referral entry 'answer' ke liye padhi gayi) toh refresh mat karo -- woh read hua hi nahi. Debatable hai, lekin 'jo diya hi nahi woh use nahi hua' simple rule hai. (3) getNegative mein bhi same karo, warna negative entries purane order mein rehengi. (4) Read ab ek write hai -- Map par chhota cost, lekin multi-threaded cache mein yahi LRU ko mehenga banata hai (lock contention); JS single-threaded hai toh yahan issue nahi.

Test: maxEntries 3, h0, h1, h2 daalo, h0 padho, phir h3 daalo. Purane behaviour mein h0 evict hota (sabse pehle insert); LRU mein h1 evict hota hai aur h0 bachta hai. Existing test 'when full, the oldest entry is evicted' tab bhi pass hona chahiye, kyunki usme koi read beech mein nahi hai.

README ko bhi update karna padega: 'NOT implemented yet' list mein LRU likha hai. Mutation check bhi jodo: getRRset wali refresh line hatao -> naya test red hona chahiye.
why_needed: Popular entries ko one-off entries ke flood se bachana -- hit rate ke liye sabse seedha sudhaar.
real_world_analogy: Library ki shelf: jo kitaab abhi kisi ne padhi, use aage rakh do; jagah chahiye toh peeche se woh kitaab hatao jise sabse lambe time se kisi ne chhua nahi.
how_it_works: getRRset hit -> positive.delete(key); positive.set(key, e) -> e Map ke end par. evict() unchanged -> pehli key = least recently used.
in_this_project: Change src/cache.ts getRRset (aur getNegative); evict() aur putRRset jaise hain waise. Naya test test/cache.test.ts ke 'cache: unit' block mein. Abhi repo mein yeh implement nahi hai -- yeh exercise hai.
advantages: Koi naya data structure nahi, Map order hi LRU list
O(1) per read
Existing tests nahi tootte
disadvantages: Har read ab write bhi hai
Scan (bahut saare one-off reads) phir bhi hot entries ko nikaal sakta hai -- LRU scan-resistant nahi
getNegative ko bhi badalna yaad rakhna
common_mistakes: Expired entry ko bhi refresh kar dena
Map.set(key, e) bina delete ke karna (order nahi badlega)
Test mein read ke baad assert karna jo read khud order badal de (assert ka order sochna)
follow_up_questions: 2Q ya ARC LRU se behtar kab hain?
Is test mein aakhri do asserts ka order ulta kar do toh kya hoga?
Multi-threaded cache mein LRU ka cost kaise kam karte hain (sampling, CLOCK)?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: LRU hit rate behtar karta hai common workloads par, keemat har read par write. JS mein sasta, multi-threaded mein contention.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Scan workload (Kaminsky-style random names) LRU ko bhi flush kar sakta hai; negative entries ka alag quota chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: CLOCK (approximate LRU), LFU, 2Q, ARC, TinyLFU (W-TinyLFU, jaise Caffeine).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x par sharded LRU (har shard ka apna Map) aur bytes-based limit; Unbound bhi slabs mein cache baant ta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Hit/miss/eviction counters, alag negative quota, aur LRU ke liye ek mutation check -- README update ke saath.

question: Two clients ask for the same uncached name at the same moment. What happens in this resolver today, why is no lock needed, and how would you add in-flight deduplication?
answer_hinglish:
Aaj: dono queries alag-alag upstream jaati hain. DnsServer har client query par resolver.resolve() bulata hai; pehli query cache miss karke await par ruk jaati hai (UDP reply ka intezaar), event loop doosri query uthata hai, woh bhi miss karta hai (pehli ka answer abhi aaya hi nahi), aur woh bhi root ya cached zone cut se poochta hai. README isse clearly likhta hai: 'No in-flight deduplication: two identical concurrent queries both go upstream.' Correctness theek hai -- dono putRRset karte hain, doosra pehle ko same rank se overwrite kar deta hai -- bas load double hai.

Lock kyun nahi chahiye: Node single-threaded hai. Map ka get aur set ke beech koi doosra code nahi chal sakta; interleaving sirf await points par hoti hai. putRRset aur getRRset ke andar koi await nahi, toh har cache operation atomic hai. Race sirf logical level par hai (check-then-fetch), data corruption nahi.

Dedupe design: Resolver mein Map<string, Promise<Resolution>> inflight, key = canonicalName|type. resolve() mein: agar key ka promise hai toh wahi await karo; warna naya promise banao, Map mein rakho, aur finally mein hata do (success ho ya failure). Dhyan: (1) Har caller ko answer ki copy do, kyunki ek shared object ko ek caller badal sakta hai. (2) Failure (SERVFAIL) bhi share hoga -- yeh theek hai, warna ek fail lookup ke peeche N retries. (3) Key mein type zaroori hai. (4) Nested NS lookups bhi dedupe se fayda le sakte hain, lekin ctx.budget per resolution hai -- shared promise ka budget pehle caller ka hai.

Multi-process (cluster) mein yeh dedupe sirf process ke andar kaam karega; across processes ke liye shared state ya consistent hashing (ek naam hamesha ek worker par) chahiye. Yeh sab is project mein implement nahi hai.
why_needed: Popular naam ke expire par thundering herd upstream servers ko unnecessary load deta hai aur spoofing ke liye bhi zyada races kholta hai (Kaminsky 'birthday' style).
real_world_analogy: Ek office mein do log ek hi waqt par canteen se chai mangwaate hain -- do peon do baar jaate hain. Dedupe: pehla peon jaa raha hai toh doosra uske haath apna order bhi bhej deta hai.
how_it_works: Today: resolve -> miss -> await upstream; second resolve -> miss -> await upstream. With dedupe: inflight.get(key) ?? (inflight.set(key, p), p.finally(() => inflight.delete(key))).
in_this_project: src/server.ts DnsServer.handle mein opts.resolver.resolve(q.name, q.type); src/resolver.ts resolve aur resolveOne; src/cache.ts mein koi await nahi. README 'NOT implemented yet': no in-flight deduplication.
advantages: Single-threaded model mein cache ko lock nahi chahiye
Dedupe chhota wrapper hai, resolver badle bina
Herd aur spoofing race window dono kam
disadvantages: Aaj duplicate upstream load
Dedupe se ek slow lookup saare waiting callers ko slow karta hai
Cross-process dedupe ke liye alag design
common_mistakes: finally mein inflight entry na hatana (failure ke baad hamesha woh promise milega)
Shared result object sab callers ko same reference dena
Key se type hata dena
follow_up_questions: Dedupe ke saath ek caller ka timeout doosre caller ko kaise affect karega?
Worker threads use karne par cache operations atomic rahenge kya?
Consistent hashing se cross-process dedupe kaise hota hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Wrapper design resolver ko untouched rakhta hai; andar (resolveOne level par) dedupe karne se nested NS lookups aur CNAME targets bhi dedupe hote, lekin budget/ctx sharing complex ho jaata hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek hung upstream lookup saare waiting callers ko latka deta hai (timeout tak); failure sab callers ko share hota hai; finally bhoolne par permanent stuck entry.
advanced.alternatives: Cache mein 'pending' entry rakhna; request coalescing at server level; Unbound jaisa mesh (har query state ek baar).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x concurrency par dedupe upstream load ko popular naamon par ek query per expiry tak le aata hai; multi-process mein per-process dedupe ya ek naam ko ek worker par route karna.
advanced.production_improvements: Dedupe + prefetch saath (popular naam kabhi cold na ho), metrics mein 'coalesced' count, aur per-caller timeouts -- sab NOT implemented.
